[2024-02-16 02:59] naph7777 : I think its generally easier to reverse engineer things. Look at teams that are doing well in your teams division (try to find one that has been at that level for a few years and is now likely moving up). Look at the players that are making them successful. Look at their evaluations, what their height/SI was at different years in HS.  From looking at a few of those work out the sort of skills you want to prioritise at different positions. Try and get on recruits that are at a similar level to those teams (who will probably be looking to upgrade what they are looking for in the future).
[2024-02-16 02:59] naph7777 : I mean you can try and work out what is undervalued in the marketplace and succeed with recruits that other people generally don't want.... but that's going to take a lot more experimentation and is generally harder to do.

[2024-05-21 11:56] thewhitehope : So quick question. When you're looking at the interested schools of a recruit it has them listed by high medium low and none interest. [2024-05-21 11:58] naph7777 : Order is random when at the same rank. If you refresh the page a few times you can often see the order change. Your knowledge of your interest (High, High++, High++, Very High) is known, but it is unknown for your opponents.

[2024-06-10 18:34] maverick1993 : What are the rules for contacts with non-seniors? I thought I heard they can only get so far and then you are wasting contacts
[2024-06-10 18:55] infinite_tea : It's a giant mystery
[2024-06-10 18:56] infinite_tea : Most people tend to agree it matters, but it gets incrementally smaller.

[2024-06-10 18:57] infinite_tea : A separate question: Does anyone know if recruiting future players hurts current chances? For instance, does recruiting a future JuCo FR Center hurt your chances with a current HS SR Center?
[2024-06-10 18:59] _plokmijn : I don’t think so. It’s only players on your roster (and impacted by positional proficiency, not where you intend on using the player)
[2024-06-10 20:24] maverick1993 : Based on the response, I don’t think I asked the right questions. I heard that if you use contacts on HS FR, SO or JR’s they cap out at like medium or something and it’s not worth putting any more contacts on them until they are seniors?
[2024-06-10 20:44] lassoball : The way I understand it is after you put a certain number of contacts into a non-SR recruit in a given year, they build interest for the rest of that year at a markedly slower rate.     Nobody knows exactly how many contacts it takes to get to diminishing returns, but I’ve seen people say roughly 20 contacts per season for non-SR player.  So, they don’t really cap out at Medium, they just don’t go much further up past the current level once you put X number of contacts in.     Whether it’s worth it to go past that invisible cap really depends on the player and a manager’s personal approach.  You don’t have to wait until they’re SRs for those contacts to become more effective again (they should move the needle better the following season).  Also, you can sometimes brute force your way past the current level, like if you want to get to the next main level of interest  (Ex: Low++ to Medium).  There are also people who believe that even if you can’t get to the next level with over-cap contacts that you might still see some of that benefit the next season when recruit interest increases/decreases with the flip.  I (stupidly) tried to blow past the cap on one guy at Medium++, only to get to Very High (with promotion) after the flip, but nobody knows exactly how all these things interact and every situation will be different.

[2024-07-29 19:05] thewhitehope : As general advice to a new player (which I am too) the comments on recruits are most important imo. They tell you what the player will be good or excellent at and what they will not be good at. You want good comments on your players.  Also look at potential, a 10 pot with really good comments is okay but you probably don't want a team full of 10 pots because they cap out sooner. Also, pay attention to how much they have improved in hs each year as that gives you an idea of how much they might improve in college. Did he go up 20 each year or only 8?

Just as in real basketball, where there is some uncertainty about a player's talent level, in Hardwood there is also built-in uncertainty in displayed skill levels. [2025-01-21 17:05] _plokmijn : They will be, but there is an additional penalty against LL5 and LL6 teams for 4 and 5 star recruits. Your 3 stars and below will lose some interest, but you also get some back during the offseason because the points you already spent appreciate in value so to speak. So you could even end up with higher interest by the start of next season despite demoting. Depends on a lot of variables like your coaching staff, how receptive the recruit is to your school, how many players your RS, how old your roster is, and more. I would focus on recruiting players with little to no other interest so that you can see the effects in your first offseason without having to worry about competing against other schools

[2025-02-11 14:24] me3too2 : How much do you care about the "be a bit sluggish" and "prone to mental mistakes" when it comes to evaluating a prospect? Is that something that is a deal-breaker as much as things like "poor defender" and "below avg ball handler"?
[2025-02-11 14:33] gards710 : for some positions (mainly on the perimeter), yes, it's a dealbreaker. for bigs, it's not for me
[2025-02-11 14:41] naph7777 : You can mitigate both "prone to mental mistakes" and "below avg ball handler" on guys who are good offensively. If they've been told to hunt their own shot then there isn't much thinking required, and similarly less dribbling as well.  Those attributes are worse on guys that can't score. Because you're telling them not to shoot, which means they will dribble more and then have to decide what play to make.
[2025-02-11 14:45] naph7777 : guards in particular seem to create better shots if they have some handling though.
[2025-02-11 14:45] gards710 : while I somewhat agree with Naph, I think that the players who are given the negative green light probably handle the ball less in general too, whereas players with a positive green light likely have the ball in their hands more. And thus the opportunities for mistakes correspondly goes down or up, respectively

[2025-03-13 07:48] juema : It's usually like this and it's easier to see if you use metric system:  Initial height <165cm (5'5") = +18cm (7 inches)  Initial height 166cm (5'5½") to 178cm (5'10") = +19cm (7,5 inches)  Initial height >179cm (5'11") = +20cm (8 inches) or +21cm (8,5 inches)  There are some exceptions (ie: 163cm growing just 17cm and 171cm growing 20cm) and sometimes taller players stay shorter of what they should, but always grow at least 18cm (7 inches).

[2025-10-31 18:24] kcb76_58795 : When the recruit I've been contacting since he was 14 shows up at school:
[2025-10-31 18:25] _plokmijn : Things I think about in that scenario: - Do I want this player? I’ve pulled scholarships late on guys I had been on for multiple seasons just because their dev wasn’t what I was hoping for or my priorities changed.   - How much have I spent vs how much is this player actually worth?  - What is my plan for this roster spot if I don’t land this player? Will my backup options mostly be gone if I wait another week? Does this scholarship need to be filled this class or am I able to regroup and find a replacement next season?  - How many open scholarships do I have next class/what is my board looking like? Am I ahead on future classes? Chasing a player might keep you from getting ahead on future recruiting   I’m sure there’s plenty of other considerations I didn’t list. But essentially just need to step back and see where you’re at overall, and figure out if it’s in your best interest to take that recruit
[2025-10-31 18:26] ryanphi : and then taking a good look at your oppenents board and trying to estimate how many points they have dropped.

[2025-11-28 18:13] flushednevada : <@595433083012907014> have you noticed the impact of the 5 star RS penalty start to decay at all for WVU?
[2025-11-28 18:17] creekcat11 : what is the RS penalty? is it from rs'ing 4 and 5 star players only?
[2025-11-28 18:22] flushednevada : The penalty makes it more difficult to build interest on recruits. I think there is technically a RS penalty for 3 stars, but it’s negligible so presidents don’t tend to avoid it.   The largest penalty comes from redshirting a 5 star, smaller from a 4 star, and so on. But it impacts all recruits. So if you redshirt a 5 star it will be harder to build interest on all targets, although I believe 5 and 4 stars are more heavily effected.  Over time the penalty fades. I’ve heard it takes a few seasons. Hopefully that helps a bit, at least as a summary.
[2025-11-28 18:25] alek9149 : Welp thats why nobody want to join Oberlin , last season im RS a 3star
[2025-11-28 18:28] flushednevada : Probably not the case - 3 Star RS penalty exists, but it’s very small. Other factors like team competition at a position, league level, in region v in state v out of region - that will all probably explain any challenges you are having.  Sometimes recruits just don’t like your team, I’ve run into that before.

OU was dominant at this time and still running the wishbone, which i still love. Our tickets were for the very top row, like literally dangerous for a kid or a drunk to be near. But the stadium was damn empty. For pregame, we went down to the first row. I actually had a practice punt bounce into my hands. I handed it back to an OU player named Hall I believe,  and I think he was convicted of murder a couple years later. Anyways, we never left the seats, and stayed in the front row.  It was a day game on Halloween weekend, and I think actually Halloween.   My dad apparently heard from others that the late night event was going on. It wasn't Late Night at the Phog and a giant production back then, it was Midnight Madness, and more or less a scrimmage. I dont know what we did between the game and Midnight Madness, but I'll never forget my first time in Allen Fieldhouse.

[2025-12-06 04:41] naph7777 : I think the real takeaway here is that particularly if the plan is just to stick a big at C on "I" offensive focus, they really don't need that many skills. I think its also worth getting a lower SI big like this early in your management career. [2025-12-06 13:29] _plokmijn : Guards: Min 10 POT in rare cases, but almost all of your guards should be 11+ POT. Min SI really depends on how much playing time you anticipate having for that player. For a low cost backup option, the 80-90 SI range and 11+ POT is where you should look but you typically need to look for 90+ SI to find multi-year starters. I don’t go for lower SI guards often, but here’s a couple examples.  82 SI 12 POT, 22.0mpg: https://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/94118 83 SI 11 POT, 10.9mpg: https://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/212859  Bigs: Min 9 POT. 65+ SI is all fair game. You can get elite bigs if you know what to look for. I’m battling Trine for a 9 POT big this cycle.   64 SI 11 POT 19.0 mpg: https://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/163869 69 SI 10 POT 21.2 mpg: https://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/168915 70 SI 11 POT 26.8 mpg: https://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/143412 73 SI 12 POT 22.8 mpg: https://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/154939 83 SI 9 POT 18.3 mpg: https://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/141619  In all cases, pay close attention to the dev rate. Low SI prospects only work out if they are able to reach their potential.

[2026-01-31 00:20] nikebones : Any general tips for recruiting for a new player? The team I chose is losing 2/3 of the roster this season, so I need to add quite a few players this year. Thanks all!
[2026-01-31 01:24] naph7777 : Use the rankings page to look at the top teams at your level. Get a feel for what attributes seem to be successful at each position (including height. Would recommend noting Spd in particular).   Look at some individual players to get an idea of how profession through HS and through college goes.  If you do that, you’ll have an idea of what to recruit and what it looks like in HS.  On player pages there is the “Development Graph”. Looking through some of those on players who ended up with high attributes is also pretty useful.
[2026-01-31 01:26] naph7777 : Without doing all that.  Get a big guy who can score a bit inside and rebound.   Get a PG (someone with positive passing, handling and preferably speed evaluation comments)  Build out from there.
[2026-01-31 01:49] nikebones : Gotcha, thanks for all this. And thanks for the tip on the development graph, I must have missed that earlier today.
[2026-01-31 01:51] nikebones : I feel like I'm pretty behind on most of the players, is it common to flip a recruit that has say, medium interest for another school? I've only been targeting 2-3 stars that have no interest or low interest so far
[2026-01-31 02:49] naph7777 : Its possible, but generally not worth it. Generally I'd advise hoarding your contacts and just looking for a bit. Try and get some guys for cheap later in this cycle. Use your bank of contacts to start getting ahead on JR's or SO's. Whilst you may think this will slow your rebuild down, I think it actually speeds you up. You get in good recruiting patterns rather than just chasing the next class repeatedly.

[2026-02-02 18:01] cdilks : I took over a team in a similar spot last season, so here is my thought process. Step 1 is accepting that you're in for a multi-season rebuild regardless of what you do. Next, I wouldn't fill all 9 scholarships this season. Long-term it will be easier if you have more balanced recruiting classes. I had 10 open spots last year, and I ended up taking six recruits. Two of those freshmen are playing this year, and the four guys with higher ceilings are redshirting. Then, of my four remaining open scholarships, I'll use two this year, and two next year. It really helps to map out your future depth charts so you know what you'll need and how many scholarships you'll have open.
[2026-02-02 18:09] cdilks : As for recruiting, my general rule was to work as cheap as possible for the first class, since I was starting late, so I didn't want to get into battles with anyone else. Stick to guys with no interest and see if you can find some interesting but imperfect players that you can pick up for a point or two, and then invest the extra points into future classes. It looks intimidating, like everyone else is getting all the good players, but there's enough talent out there to put together a good D2/D3 team with leftovers. There's really no point to tactical game-planning with your roster for a few seasons, so spend that extra time combing through recruit pages.

[2026-03-25 13:03] naph7777 : This is actually pretty instructive for others. Drip-feeding recruits, especially early in the season is really not a good strategy. Other people can't tell if you're Medium-flat, or 1 contact away from High.  Also by investing in multiple targets this year, other teams that may have been watching guys you were at Medium on, will be able to tell that you have spread your points around and that you would struggle to get ahead if they jumped straight to High.  In general, early season recruiting strategy is either, go hard early to scare people off..... or have a number of targets, wait and see what others do until just before your target can start committing (Day 5 for HS SR, 10 for JuCO, 15 for INTL) and then jump them up to at least High in 1 swoop. Having targets at Medium rather than High, and then also spending recruits on other targets is asking for trouble.

[2026-04-02 03:08] naph7777 : My general rule of thumb is Stamina+20 minutes, you can probably bump that up down by roughly your team's pace, or maybe up/down by half your team's pace. (so +2 pace means cut their mins by 1).... but generally you just experiment and find the line where they are Low fatigue in most games.
[2026-04-02 03:08] tony9955. : Thank you
[2026-04-02 03:09] naph7777 : There's a small drop off in performance with fatigue, bust mostly you just want to avoid the overworked penalty.
[2026-04-02 03:28] swarm4 : What’s the negatives of having moderate fatigue most games
[2026-04-02 03:28] swarm4 : Like if a guy has light/moderate fatigue most games. Sometimes has heavy, sometimes has none. What’re the long term ramifications of that
[2026-04-02 03:29] naph7777 : You run the risk of player becoming overworked. Which is an ongoing debuff that can be removed if you treat it like an injury and they have time off until its gone, but generally it remains for the rest of the season.
[2026-04-02 03:31] naph7777 : "- Overwork As the season progresses, overworked players who log close to 40 minutes per game (i.e. without much rest) or play through elevated fatigue levels will see their performance decline in subsequent games. This decreased effectiveness will continue until the end of the season." - [rules](https://onlinecollegebasketball.org/rules)

[2026-04-08 22:48] bengalman : I suggest that you should have your scholarships spread 3-2-3-2-3, so right now you should be looking for 3 HS/INTL players to redshirt next season. [2026-04-08 22:52] gwhiz5 : Everything you said is helpful, thank you. My only other question is how is the whole red shirt thing work?
[2026-04-08 22:53] gwhiz5 : Also, you think it’s good to bring in just 3 freshman total?
[2026-04-08 22:55] bengalman : Ok, a redshirt is super simple. You can redshirt a player anytime during their FR/SO/JR year with one hitch, they can only play in up to 5 games. In exchange for them not playing a year they don't lose that year of eligibility. So its another year of them in college developing they just can't play really.
[2026-04-08 22:55] gwhiz5 : Ahh ok
[2026-04-08 22:56] gwhiz5 : Makes sense
[2026-04-08 22:58] bengalman : 3 HS SR that can come in and be the redshirting guys next year should be the #1 focus right now, along with a new head coach. These 3 will hopefully become the guys who get you out of D3 and hopefully D1. If you want to fill out the roster more you can but be careful with using up too many scholarships. If you spend all 10 this year, you will only have 1 for next season and zero the year after that.
